description: Indian Railways is the fourth-largest national railway network in the world. For administrative convenience and efficient management, it is divided into 19 distinct Railway Zones across the country.

sections.title: Historical Background
sections.description: The Indian railway system was introduced during the British era, primarily to facilitate the transport of raw materials and troops.

historical_events.significance: Ran between Bombay (Bori Bunder) and Thane, covering a distance of 34 km. It was hauled by three steam locomotives: Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan.
Ran between Bombay VT and Kurla on the Harbour Line. It was famously named the 'Deccan Queen'.
Post-independence, the diverse railway systems were nationalized and integrated into a single state-owned enterprise, Indian Railways.

important_facts.fact: Lord Dalhousie is widely regarded as the 'Father of Indian Railways' for initiating the railway network in the country.

sections.title: Railway Gauge System
sections.description: The clear minimum perpendicular distance between the inner faces of the two tracks is called a Railway Gauge. India primarily uses three types of gauges.

key_concepts.explanation: The distance between the tracks is 1.676 meters (5 ft 6 in). Over 90% of the Indian rail network operates on broad gauge, which is being standardized under 'Project Unigauge'.
The distance between the tracks is exactly 1.000 meter. These are gradually being phased out and converted into broad gauge lines.
The distance between the tracks is 0.762 meters or 0.610 meters. It is predominantly used in mountainous terrains and heritage railway lines.

sections.title: Major Railway Zones and Headquarters
sections.description: Indian Railways is divided into 19 zones (including the Metro Railway, Kolkata). Matching zones with their headquarters is a frequent exam question.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the largest railway zone in India in terms of route kilometers.
It operates some of the most heavily congested suburban train networks in the country.
It was the first railway zone formed in independent India (in 1951).
Also established in 1951, it was one of the earliest zones created post-independence.
It is the 18th railway zone of India, officially announced in 2019 by carving out parts of the East Coast and South Central Railways.
Kolkata Metro is India's only urban rapid transit system that enjoys the status of an independent railway zone (the 17th zone, added in 2010).
It achieved the milestone of becoming India's first 100% electrified railway zone.

sections.title: Major Manufacturing Units
sections.description: Indian Railways operates several in-house industrial units that manufacture locomotives, passenger coaches, and wheels.

key_associations.extra_info: This facility manufactured India's first indigenous semi-high-speed train, the Vande Bharat Express (Train 18).
It is one of the largest electric locomotive manufacturers in the world.
It is the primary manufacturer of the advanced LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch) coaches used in Rajdhani and Shatabdi trains.
It is the newest and most technologically advanced coach manufacturing unit of Indian Railways.
It produces train wheels, axles, and wheelsets using advanced cast steel technology.

sections.title: Important Geographical Rail Projects
sections.description: Due to India's varied topography, several specialized railway corridors and engineering marvels have been constructed.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: A 760 km long engineering marvel running parallel to the Arabian Sea coastline through the rugged Western Ghats, featuring over 2000 bridges and 91 tunnels.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: EDFC (Punjab to West Bengal) & WDFC (UP to Maharashtra)
geographical_data.key_characteristics: High-speed and high-capacity railway corridors exclusively meant for the transportation of freight, aimed at decongesting passenger networks.
It is the world's highest railway arch bridge, standing 359 meters above the Chenab riverbed, connecting the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial superlatives and one-liner static GK facts frequently asked in competitive exams regarding Indian Railways.

important_facts.fact: The Vivek Express, which runs from Dibrugarh (Assam) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu), covers the longest train route in India (approximately 4,189 km).
Shree Siddharoodha Swamiji Hubballi Junction in Karnataka has the world's longest railway platform, measuring 1,507 meters in length.
The Bogibeel Bridge in Assam, built over the Brahmaputra River, is India's longest rail-cum-road bridge (4.94 km).

Four Indian Railways sites are designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, Nilgiri Mountain Railway, Kalka-Shimla Railway, and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT).
